changes.title: New page header and color palette
changes.what_why: The navy header bar and grey tables are replaced by a lighter header and one set of colors shared by buttons, badges and links.

changes.title: Reading font and larger type
changes.what_why: Everything was 13px Verdana, so titles and body text looked alike. Titles now use a book serif and body text is 16px.

changes.title: Search moves to the top of the page
changes.what_why: Search was a small box in the corner of the header. On the catalogue it is now the first thing on the page, with a larger field.

changes.title: Availability badges
changes.what_why: Availability showed as status codes like IN and OUT (2 HLD). Each title now has a badge that says Available or Checked out, with the number of holds waiting.

changes.title: “Place hold” button replaces the Hold link
changes.what_why: The small “Hold” link did not look clickable, and testers missed it. It is now a button that says what it does.

changes.title: Results as cards with covers
changes.what_why: Results were a dense seven-column table. They are now cards with a cover, author and availability, which scan faster and fit a phone screen.

changes.title: Format filter chips
changes.what_why: Filtering by format meant opening Advanced search. Chips under the search box now filter by Book, eBook or Audiobook in one click.

changes.title: Plain-language due dates
changes.what_why: Due dates appeared as 2026-10-14. They now read “Due back Oct 14”.

changes.title: Upcoming events strip
changes.what_why: Events were only listed on a separate page. The catalogue now shows the next three, so people looking for books also see what is on.

changes.title: “Open now” in the header
changes.what_why: Opening hours were only in the footer. The header now says whether the library is open, and until when.

changes.title: Larger cover and a details grid
changes.what_why: The cover was a 60px thumbnail next to a run-on paragraph of details. The cover is now larger and the details sit in a labeled grid.

changes.title: Explain the hold queue
changes.what_why: The page said “2 HLD” without saying what that means for you. It now says where you would be in line and roughly how long you would wait.

changes.title: More by this author
changes.what_why: Adds a row of the author’s other titles to the bottom of the book page.

changes.title: One h1 per page, headings in order
changes.what_why: No page had an h1. Titles were h3 and section headings skipped levels. Each page now has one h1, and headings step down in order.
changes.no_preview_reason: Invisible by design: headings keep their size and color. Only the HTML level changed, which screen readers and the page outline use.

changes.title: Names for icon-only buttons
changes.what_why: Screen readers announced the search and account buttons only as “button”. They are now announced as “Search the catalogue” and “Your account”.

changes.title: Confirm holds without reloading the page
changes.what_why: Placing a hold reloaded the page and dropped you back at the top. Now the button changes to “Hold placed” and a short message confirms it.
changes.no_preview_reason: This changes what happens after a click. Place a hold on the stable and redesign servers to compare.

changes.title: Faster paging through results
changes.what_why: Every page of results ran the whole search again. Results are now kept for a few minutes, so the next page opens straight away.
changes.no_preview_reason: Server-side only. The page looks the same, so compare paging speed on the two servers.
